findings.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — (P1, confidence 100) The read-then-unconditional `await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: user.id }, data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) } })` admits two concurrent requests with the same backup code because both authenticate against the pre-consumption blob before either write commits, granting two login sessions for a code promised to be single-use.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — [P1, confidence 100] The backup-code feature has no executable verification for backup-code login, one-time rejection, or backup-code 2FA disable—the diff itself leaves `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`—so regressions in the primary recovery flows ship undetected.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — [P1, confidence 100] `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"));` rejects when clipboard permission is denied, yet the unconditional success toast reports the recovery codes were copied even though no usable copy exists.

apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:148 — [P2, confidence 100] `const res = await signIn<"credentials">("credentials", {` rejects on a login network failure without a catch, leaving the user with no error state or failure message.

packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — [P2, confidence 75] The unrelated global change `tabIndex={-1}` removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField consumer, and the strongest rebuttal—that it prevents focus interference in the new 2FA modal—fails because the shared component change alters all existing password forms rather than scoping that behavior to the modal.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — [P1; confidence 100] `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(...); const index = backupCodes.indexOf(...); ... await prisma.user.update(...)` performs a non-atomic read-then-write, so concurrent login requests carrying the same valid backup code both pass verification and create authenticated sessions before either request consumes it.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — [P1; confidence 100] The suite leaves backup-code login and backup-code 2FA disabling unexercised (`// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`), so either implementation can reject valid codes or accept invalid ones while the changed E2E suite passes.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:116 — [P2; confidence 100] The download test asserts only `expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toBe("cal-backup-codes.txt")`, so it passes when the feature downloads an empty or stale file instead of the generated backup codes.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:122 — [P2; confidence 100] The copy test verifies only `await page.getByTestId("toast-success").waitFor()` after clicking, so it passes when the UI reports success without placing any backup codes on the clipboard.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces significant new backup code functionality (login with backup codes, disabling 2FA with backup codes, backup code generation and display) but the test file explicitly contains a TODO comment at line 12 stating 'TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The existing tests only verify backup code download/copy/close UI interactions but don't test the actual authentication flows using backup codes. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial security-critical logic, not a bug but an important missing test concern grounded in the specific diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — [P1, confidence 100] `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"));` rejects when clipboard permission is denied, yet the unconditional success toast reports the recovery codes were copied even though no usable copy exists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 278: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"));` followed immediately by `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success");`. The clipboard API returns a Promise that can reject if permission is denied or the operation fails, but the code doesn't await it or handle errors - it unconditionally shows a success toast. This is a real bug where users could see 'Backup codes copied!' even when the copy operation failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — [P2, confidence 75] The unrelated global change `tabIndex={-1}` removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField consumer, and the strongest rebuttal—that it prevents focus interference in the new 2FA modal—fails because the shared component change alters all existing password forms rather than scoping that behavior to the modal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows adding tabIndex={-1} to the password visibility toggle button in the shared PasswordField component at line 50. This is a real change that affects all consumers of PasswordField, not just the 2FA modal. The finding correctly identifies that this removes the button from keyboard navigation globally. While this could be intentional UX (users typically don't need to tab to the show/hide password button), it's a valid architectural concern that a shared component change affects all existing password forms. This is a scope/architecture concern rather than a bug since the button still works via mouse click.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — [P1; confidence 100] `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(...); const index = backupCodes.indexOf(...); ... await prisma.user.update(...)` performs a non-atomic read-then-write, so concurrent login requests carrying the same valid backup code both pass verification and create authenticated sessions before either request consumes it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a read-then-write pattern in next-auth-options.ts lines 139-152: backup codes are decrypted and parsed, then checked with indexOf, then the array is modified and written back with prisma.user.update. This is indeed non-atomic - two concurrent requests with the same valid backup code could both read the same backup codes array, both find the code at the same index, both pass verification, and then both write back (with only one code removed). This is a real race condition that could allow a backup code to be used twice for authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — [P1; confidence 100] The suite leaves backup-code login and backup-code 2FA disabling unexercised (`// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`), so either implementation can reject valid codes or accept invalid ones while the changed E2E suite passes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup code functionality for both login and 2FA disabling, but the test file explicitly contains a TODO comment at line 12 acknowledging missing test coverage: '// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The new backup code logic in next-auth-options.ts (login) and totp/disable.ts is non-trivial security code that validates backup codes, removes used codes, and handles error cases. While some backup code UI tests exist (download, copy, close buttons), the actual authentication flow using backup codes is not tested. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added security-critical functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:116 — [P2; confidence 100] The download test asserts only `expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toBe("cal-backup-codes.txt")`, so it passes when the feature downloads an empty or stale file instead of the generated backup codes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 116 only checks the filename of the downloaded file, not its content. The TODO comment in the diff at line 119 ('// TODO: check file content') confirms this is a known gap. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added backup code functionality - the test could pass even if the download contains wrong or empty content. However, this is not a bug in the feature itself, but rather incomplete test coverage for new functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:122 — [P2; confidence 100] The copy test verifies only `await page.getByTestId("toast-success").waitFor()` after clicking, so it passes when the UI reports success without placing any backup codes on the clipboard.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 122 only verifies that a toast success message appears after clicking the copy button, but does not actually verify that the backup codes were placed on the clipboard. Looking at the diff, the test code shows: `await page.getByTestId("backup-codes-copy").click(); await page.getByTestId("toast-success").waitFor(); // TODO: check clipboard content`. The TODO comment in the test itself acknowledges this limitation. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality - the copy feature could show success without actually copying anything, and the test wouldn't catch it. This is an important non-bug issue about incomplete test coverage for new functionality.
